findings.note: Cycle 5: confirmed asymmetric guard; added 'expired'. Validated.

OWNER ANSWERED 2026-06-16: MULTI-FIELD SPLIT ORDERS ARE REAL (an order can span several fields with different customer ownership per field). Therefore the prescribed fix (flat per-customer Hamilton + require sum=100) is WRONG — it assumes a single field where customer pcts sum to 100. CORRECT FIX = redesign to allocate PER FIELD: split each field's portion of the order by THAT field's customer splits, then sum per customer. This needs field->line attribution (the function currently applies a flat per-customer total_pct to every line with NO per-field line breakdown), so it is a deeper redesign than the original finding implied — re-scope before building. Still dormant on live (0 split invoices ever, 0 multi-field quotes today). ORIGINAL ANALYSIS: Penny-drift is real (each customer's per-line share is round()'d independently -> sum can != line total). The Hamilton fix is designed (calculate_billing_splits(line_cents, pcts[]) per line, item-outer/customer-inner restructure; full draft in REMEDIATION-HANDOFF). BLOCKER: get_field_billing_splits_for_order SUMS split_pct per customer ACROSS fields (orders->quote_sections->field_billing_defaults). Single-field order: pcts sum to 100 (Hamilton + sum=100 guard correct). MULTI-FIELD order: per-customer summed pct can be !=100 (e.g. 2 fields each 100%/different customer -> sum=200); the original then bills each customer their FULL summed pct of every line (double-bill), and BOTH the Hamilton fix AND the sum=100 guard change/break that. Needs Mason's business answer: are split invoices only for single-field orders, or must multi-field allocate differently? LIVE TODAY: 4 fbd rows/3 fields all sum to 100, 0 multi-field quotes, 1 order w/ quote, 0 split invoices ever -> bug dormant, guard safe today but feature is dark. Defer until semantics resolved.
